outline_section.section_title: Introduction to Automobile Motion as a System
outline_section.learning_goal: Define automobile motion as a system by identifying a physical input signal, a physical output signal, and the rule that maps one to the other through kinematic integration.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Simple one-dimensional car-motion schematic showing position x(t), velocity v(t), and acceleration a(t) signals with arrows indicating input and output pairing and one integrator block.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Minimal line-art diagram only, with no decorative elements. Emphasize the mapping direction between chosen signals.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Show that automobile motion examples are input-output systems by naming one physical input and one physical output and expressing the system rule as a derivative/integral relation.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use a no-slope-motion case with constant input acceleration $a(t)=a_0$ and zero initial velocity/position so $v(t)=a_0 t$, $x(t)=\frac12 a_0 t^2$.
paragraph_plan: Define the core system viewpoint for motion: a mapping from one motion-related quantity over time to another.
Introduce common candidates for input and output signals: acceleration, velocity, and position.
State the kinematic operator relations that connect them, emphasizing that the same physical setup can be expressed with different chosen pairs.
Close by previewing upcoming sections: selecting valid pairs, then applying single and double integration.

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: For a car with constant acceleration input $a(t)=2\,\mathrm{m/s}^2$, choose input and output signals to model one system rule and state the rule in equation form.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Identify a valid input-output pairing and write the corresponding system mapping with the appropriate integration relation.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: The first section's base concept is converted into one explicit modeled system rule.
solution_step_plan: Identify a physical signal to treat as input (example: $a(t)$).
Write the direct rule connecting them with the chosen initial condition convention.
Check units and causality direction to keep the system orientation consistent.
practice_variation_axes: Swap which kinematic variable is treated as input
Use different constant and ramp-like input examples
Change initial-condition treatment (e.g., zero versus nonzero)

outline_section.handoff_notes: Tutorial needs a concrete schematic. Keep the first example focused: one rule only, no branching.
